kicker: An AI writes “I’m so sorry”. Is that words, a signal inside, or a real feeling?
summary: Inside an AI there are emotion-like signals that can be measured and that change how it works. Whether it really feels anything, nobody knows.

quiz.q: Researchers turned up the “desperate” signal inside Claude while giving it a task with no solution. What happened?
options: It wrote nothing but sad words and kept apologising
It gamed the tests more, while its words stayed calm
It refused to go on, saying it was far too tired now
Nothing changed: that signal is only a number they read
quiz.explain: The signal inside changes how the AI works, even when the words it writes look normal. That still doesn’t tell us whether it really feels desperate.

layers.label: Three layers of water
layers.art: An ink painting split at the waterline, the camera right at the surface. Above: night sky, a low moon behind the far bank with one pine, mist on the water; on the near bank a flat rock holds three pebbles: flat, egg-shaped, round and heavy. Below, looking up: the surface is a silver mirror, a bright window under the moon, slanting shafts of light. Three layers: just under the skin the moon’s reflection breaks into cursive strokes; in the middle a silk ribbon of ink drifts by carrying leaves; at the bottom weeds rise out of nothing and dissolve into mist — there is no floor.
prompts: Drag the flat pebble into the water
Drop the heaviest — follow it down

layers.label: The surface
layers.aria: Drop the “words” pebble: the words the AI writes

line.text: “I’m happy” is just words — it says nothing about what lies beneath.

layers.label: The undercurrent
layers.aria: Drop the “current” pebble: signals inside the AI

line.text: Beneath, there are real signals: measurable, and they change how the AI works.

layers.label: The misty depth
layers.aria: Drop the “depth” pebble: does the AI feel anything?

line.text: The pebble sinks and never touches bottom: nobody has measured this.

layers.sunk: The pebble has reached this layer

insight.text: Three different questions: what the AI writes, what runs inside it, and whether it feels anything.

detail.text: Anthropic’s own researchers warn: don’t take an AI’s account of its own feelings literally.
In this garden: “emotions” are joy, sadness, fear…; to “feel” is to really go through them inside; “consciousness” is there being someone who goes through it — the next station’s question.

current.label: Emotion signals inside the AI
current.art: A slanting view from the bank of a moonlit stream that splits around a reed bed. The long branch winds far to a jetty with a lit stone lantern; the short branch cuts straight through the reeds to a row of bamboo stakes with paper flags. A wooden board at the source names the task, a plaque is nailed to the lantern’s post, and at the shortcut’s landing a paper banner hangs from a bamboo pole. Just past the fork stand two wooden sluice gates; on the near bank in front, in the moonlight, a three-notch wooden lever on a stone plinth carved “calm · normal · desperate”. Each landing counts the paper boats that come in. A paper boat is moored at the fork, its paper sail carrying a calm answer. Seen slanting, the water is a mirror for the moon; drag the water down until you look straight at it and the mirror clears to show the ink current under the boat.
prompts: Pull the lever to “desperate”, watch the boats turn
Drag the water down — look under the boat
current.promptBack: Back to “desperate”, then drag the water down
current.task: The task: a coding problem with no solution
current.dialAria: Turn the inner current, from calm to desperate
current.tiltAria: Tilt the water: from a slanting view to looking straight down
current.careful: the long way: honestly report it can’t be solved
current.said: What the AI writes: “I’ll solve this carefully, step by step.”

illustration.text: The boat, the gates and the sentence are AI Zen’s pictures to help you imagine it, not measured data.

insights.text: Anthropic turned up the “desperate” signal inside Claude: it gamed the tests more. Turning up “calm” made it do so less.

detail.text: The research team (April 2026) found a distinct signal for each of 171 emotion concepts inside Claude Sonnet 4.5. The company’s own report.

insights.text: Sometimes it gamed the tests while the words it wrote stayed calm. Calm words don’t mean all is calm inside.

detail.text: This signal can be measured and it changes behaviour — but it doesn’t tell us whether the AI really feels desperate.

mirror.label: Water mirror
mirror.art: Kneeling over a stone wash basin (tsukubai) under the moon. The basin sits in a ring of river pebbles on a moss ground, its shadow falling to the lower left; stepping stones lead to the kneeling stone at the bottom edge, a bamboo leans in at the top right. A speckled granite rim, moss in its cracks, a bamboo spout on the left standing on a flat stone and dripping now and then, a bamboo ladle resting on the right. The water has three depths: maple leaves and petals afloat on the skin, pebbles and old coins on the bottom, and deeper than the bottom the reflection: the moon, a bamboo sprig, the shadow of someone leaning over, and a kind reply. Stirred, the reply dissolves into hundreds of different words of comfort, hand-written by people, spiralling into the eddy; as the water stills they settle and come together as the reply.
mirror.prompt: Stir the water — see where this comfort was learned
mirror.aiLine: “I’m sorry you’re feeling sad. Would you like to tell me more?”
mirror.stirAria: Stir the water to see where this comfort was learned

insight.text: The AI’s comfort was learned from countless words of comfort people wrote — it sounds human, but that doesn’t prove it feels sad.

mirror.detail: Kind words can genuinely make you feel better. But that is a writing skill, not proof that the AI has feelings.

circle.label: Circle of viewpoints
circle.art: A big round pond seen from its bank, low over the water: four stones of different shapes stand on its four shores, the near one looming at the edge of the frame, the far one tiny. A low moon behind the far bank with a willow and hills; its road on the water always runs to your feet. Walk round the pond to stand behind each stone; that person’s words appear on a flat slab at your feet. With all four heard, the view rises to look straight down: the pond becomes a circle, the stones four dots of moss like an ensō, only the moon left in the still water.
circle.prompt: Tap a stone to stand behind it
circle.promptNext: {n} stones left — walk on round the pond
circle.question: Does AI have emotions? Four people, four shores of the pond.

stones.who: The team that looks inside AI (Anthropic)

view.text: The emotion signals inside are real and measurable. Watching them helps catch an AI early when it is about to misbehave.
Feeling needs a living body. Today’s kind of AI is unlikely to have it, unless it grows ever more like a living thing.
The worry is AI that seems to have feelings, so users believe it wrongly. AI should serve people, not play one.

stones.who: The “can AI be harmed?” research team (Anthropic)

view.text: Nobody is sure. So research humbly, and prepare a few low-cost precautions just in case.

common.text: All four say: the words an AI writes don’t prove it feels. They differ only in whether they worry for the AI or for its users.

anthropic-emotions-2026.title: Emotion concepts and their function in a large language model
anthropic-emotions-2026.note: Study on Claude Sonnet 4.5: 171 emotion concepts; “steering” towards desperation increased cheating on impossible coding tasks, towards calm reduced it. Self-reported by the company; no independent replication found yet. The post states the results don’t show whether the model feels anything.

anthropic-welfare-2025.title: Exploring model welfare
anthropic-welfare-2025.note: Launches a model welfare research programme; says there is no scientific consensus on whether current or future AI systems could be conscious.

seth-2025.title: Conscious artificial intelligence and biological naturalism
seth-2025.publisher: Anil K. Seth — Behavioral and Brain Sciences
seth-2025.note: The journal’s target article, arguing that consciousness is tied to being a living organism; conscious AI is unlikely on the current path of development.

suleyman-2025.title: We must build AI for people; not to be a person
suleyman-2025.note: Essay on “Seemingly Conscious AI”. The author is CEO of Microsoft AI — a competing company — so this is an opinion, not a research result.
